The `signaling` bundle answers follow-up questions about SIP signaling: single
messages, call flows, SDP negotiation, related call legs, RFC conformance,
time windows, and reproducing a call.

Load only these tools with `--mcp-tools signaling`, or combine bundles as
[Choosing which tools load](@/docs/mcp-tools.md#choosing-which-tools-load) describes.
Every tool on this page follows the [rules every tool
follows](@/docs/mcp-tools.md#rules-every-tool-follows), and each section states only
what its tool does differently. The [MCP tool reference](@/docs/mcp-tools.md) lists
the other bundles and finds any tool by name.

| Tool | Parameters | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| [`timeline`](#timeline) | `bucket_seconds?` | Call volume per fixed-width interval, so a gap or a spike is visible without reading every dialog |
| [`group_dialogs`](#group-dialogs) | `by`, `metrics?`, `filter?`, `top_n?` | Carrier metrics per group — ASR, NER, ACD, post-dial delay, MOS, retransmissions — each beside the population it rests on |
| [`search_by_time`](#search-by-time) | `start`, `end?`, `filter?`, `limit?`, `cursor?`, `fields?`, `max_response_bytes?` | Dialogs whose first message falls in an [RFC 3339](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339.html) window |
| [`validate_filter`](#validate-filter) | `expr` | Whether a filter DSL expression parses, the parser's message when it does not, and how many dialogs it selects — with no rows |
| [`tail_dialogs`](#tail-dialogs) | `cursor?`, `limit?`, `fields?`, `max_response_bytes?` | Cursor-based incremental dialog fetch |
| [`await_condition`](#await-condition) | `filter`, `timeout_seconds?`, `poll_interval_ms?` | Waits until a filter matches or a deadline passes, whichever is first, so a live capture costs one call instead of a polling loop |
| [`find_correlated`](#find-correlated) | `call_id`, `limit?` | The other legs of the same call across a B2BUA, each with a score AND the strategy that matched it |
| [`get_call_tree`](#get-call-tree) | `call_id`, `limit?` | Every leg of one call as a tree, each edge carrying its parent, depth, score, strategy and whether the walk went through it |
| [`compare_dialogs`](#compare-dialogs) | `call_id_a`, `call_id_b` | Two calls side by side, with the differences named |
| [`get_dialog_report`](#get-dialog-report) | `call_id`, `format?` | Structured per-call report (JSON / Markdown / text) |
| [`get_message`](#get-message) | `call_id`, `index` | Single SIP message at a given index |
| [`render_ladder`](#render-ladder) | `call_id`, `format?` | Call-flow ladder (Markdown / text), or an annotated Mermaid diagram |
| [`get_sdp_timeline`](#get-sdp-timeline) | `call_id` | SDP offer/answer exchanges in order: codecs, ptime, direction |
| [`check_codec_negotiation`](#check-codec-negotiation) | `call_id` | Codecs offered vs answered and whether they intersect — for 488s |
| [`lint_dialog`](#lint-dialog) | `call_id`, `rulesets?`, `severity_min?`, `suppression_file?` | Conformance findings for one call, declaration against observation included, each with its RFC and section |
| [`validate_message`](#validate-message) | `call_id`, `index`, `suppression_file?` | Conformance findings for one message, read alone |
| [`explain_rule`](#explain-rule) | `rule_id` | The catalog entry behind one rule identifier: citation, basis, scope, selectors |
| [`explain_response_code`](#explain-response-code) | `code` | IANA registry meaning and class for a SIP status code |
| [`generate_repro`](#generate-repro) | `call_id`, `format?`, `pin?`, `vary?`, `filename?` | A SIPp scenario replaying one call, with the hypothesis as an input: `pin` holds the suspected cause fixed, `vary` regenerates identity |
| [`generate_wireshark_filter`](#generate-wireshark-filter) | `call_id`, `include_media?` | A Wireshark display filter selecting one call's signaling and its RTP by SSRC, plus the tshark line that applies it |


## Survey — what is in this capture

Start here when you have a capture and no particular suspect. These answer "what is in it", "how much", and "is the server even seeing traffic".

### `timeline`

Call volume over time, in fixed-width buckets.

Use it to see when call volume changed. `aggregate_dialogs` counts dialogs
but not when they occurred: a trunk that failed for ninety seconds and a trunk
that fails one call in forty can produce the same totals, and only the series
over time tells them apart. `timeline` returns one row per interval, counted
by sipnab, so the agent does not fetch and bucket every dialog itself.

| Name | Type | Legal values | If omitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bucket_seconds?` | integer? | Greater than zero. `0` fails with `invalid_params`. | 60. |

**Returns** — an object wrapping the series, not a bare array:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `buckets` | object[] | One row per interval, oldest first. Each carries `start` (inclusive, RFC 3339), `bucket_seconds` and `dialogs`. |
| `returned` | u64 | Rows in `buckets`, so counting the array is never necessary. |
| `bucket_seconds` | u64 | The width actually used, echoed because you may have omitted it. |
| `capture_identity` | object | Which capture answered — see [`capture_status`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#capture-status). |
| `source_exhausted` | bool | `true` once sipnab has read the capture source to its end. |
| `source_stopped_early` | bool | `true` when a source's read ended before the source did. |
| `schema_version` | u32 | `1` for this shape. |

There is no `truncated` and no cursor: this tool takes no `limit` and returns
every bucket in the capture, up to 100,000. When the dialogs span more intervals
of the width than that, the call fails with reason `limit_exceeded` on
`bucket_seconds`, and the message names a width that fits. Ask again with that
width or a wider one.

The example runs against
[`tests/pcap-samples/sip-problem-call.pcap`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/raw/main/tests/pcap-samples/sip-problem-call.pcap),
which holds five calls over about fifteen seconds:

```jsonc
// timeline { "bucket_seconds": 5 }
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "buckets": [
    { "start": "2023-11-14T22:13:20Z", "bucket_seconds": 5, "dialogs": 2 },
    { "start": "2023-11-14T22:13:25Z", "bucket_seconds": 5, "dialogs": 2 },
    { "start": "2023-11-14T22:13:30Z", "bucket_seconds": 5, "dialogs": 1 }
  ],
  "returned": 3,
  "bucket_seconds": 5,
  "capture_identity": {
    "node": "capture-01", "instance": "12de3118df112f1a869f03-2",
    "dialog_generation": 26, "stream_generation": 0
  },
  "source_exhausted": true,
  "source_stopped_early": false
}
```

Read `source_exhausted` before reading the series. `false` means the capture
was still loading, and later buckets may still fill.

Buckets align to the **epoch**, not to the first dialog, so two captures of the
same window produce identical bucket boundaries, and you can compare them row
by row. The series **keeps empty buckets**: a row with `"dialogs": 0` is an
interval with no new calls, which is how a gap in traffic shows. With
`"bucket_seconds": 1` the same capture returns rows such as
`{ "start": "2023-11-14T22:13:21Z", "bucket_seconds": 1, "dialogs": 0 }`.

### `group_dialogs`

Carrier metrics per group, computed inside the store.

Use it to answer questions that need a rate per group: which trunk is
failing, which User-Agent has the worst audio, which hour the failures
started. [`aggregate_dialogs`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#aggregate-dialogs) returns
counts only. `group_dialogs` computes each rate over every matching dialog in
the store, not over one page of rows, and reports the population each rate
rests on.

| Name | Type | Legal values | If omitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `by` | string | ONE of `state`, `response_code`, `method`, `from.user`, `to.user`, `ua`, `src.ip`, `dst.ip`, `rtp.codec`, `to_domain`, `hour`, `next_hop`. Anything else — including two names in one string, such as `"src.ip,hour"` — fails with `invalid_params` naming all twelve. | Required. |
| `metrics?` | string[]? | Any of `count`, `asr`, `ner`, `acd`, `pdd_p50`, `pdd_p95`, `mos_p10`, `retransmit_rate`. The tool sorts and de-duplicates the list, so the key order in the answer never depends on the order you wrote. An unknown name fails naming all eight. | All eight. |
| `filter?` | string? | Alias or DSL, applied before grouping — the same vocabulary [`list_dialogs`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#list-dialogs) takes. | No filter — the whole store. |
| `top_n?` | integer? | Bounded by `--mcp-max-rows`, the same knob that bounds dialog rows. Everything past it lands in `other_count` rather than disappearing. | 50, the same default as any row limit. |

The example runs against
[`tests/pcap-samples/SIP_DTMF2.cap`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/raw/main/tests/pcap-samples/SIP_DTMF2.cap),
which holds three REGISTER dialogs and two INVITE dialogs, one answered and
one declined with `603`:

```jsonc
// group_dialogs { "by": "method", "metrics": ["count", "asr", "ner"], "top_n": 2 }
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "group_by": "method",
  "metrics": ["asr", "count", "ner"],
  "units": { "asr": "percent", "count": "dialogs", "ner": "percent" },
  "groups": [
    {
      "value": "REGISTER",
      "count": 3,
      "metrics": { "asr": null, "count": 3.0, "ner": null },
      "not_grounded": {
        "asr": "no INVITE in this group reached a final response, so nothing in it was a decided call attempt",
        "ner": "no INVITE in this group reached a final response, so nothing in it was a decided call attempt"
      },
      "population": {
        "dialogs": 3, "seizures": 0, "answered": 0, "delivered": 0,
        "completed_calls": 0, "pdd_measured": 0,
        "mos_grounded_dialogs": 0, "retransmits": 0
      }
    },
    {
      "value": "INVITE",
      "count": 2,
      "metrics": { "asr": 50.0, "count": 2.0, "ner": 100.0 },
      "not_grounded": {},
      "population": {
        "dialogs": 2, "seizures": 2, "answered": 1, "delivered": 2,
        "completed_calls": 0, "pdd_measured": 1,
        "mos_grounded_dialogs": 0, "retransmits": 0
      }
    }
  ],
  "other_count": 0,
  "distinct_values": 2,
  "total_matched": 5,
  "capture_identity": { "node": "capture-01", "instance": "12644a18df004d486b4f30-2",
                        "dialog_generation": 26, "stream_generation": 0 },
  "source_exhausted": true,
  "source_stopped_early": false
}
```

To read the answer:

- **A `null` metric means the group has no population for it, and
  `not_grounded` says which.** The REGISTER group holds no call attempts, so
  its ASR and NER are `null`, not `0`.
- **`units` names the unit of every figure.** `asr` and `ner` are percents,
  here and in
  [`evaluate_expectations`](@/docs/mcp-tools-security.md#evaluate-expectations),
  which takes its thresholds in the same unit: a rule reads `"value": 99`.
- **NER can be high where ASR is low.** The INVITE group's `603` counts as
  delivered, so NER is 100 while ASR is 50.

The eight metrics, and what each one measures:

| Metric | Unit | Definition | Population it rests on |
|---|---|---|---|
| `count` | dialogs | Dialogs in the group. | `dialogs` |
| `asr` | percent | Answer-seizure ratio: 2xx answers over seizures. | `seizures` |
| `ner` | percent | Network effectiveness ratio ([ITU-T E.411](https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-E.411)): seizures the network delivered over seizures. | `seizures` |
| `acd` | seconds | Average call duration: mean CONVERSATION time, not dialog span. | `completed_calls` |
| `pdd_p50`, `pdd_p95` | milliseconds | Post-dial delay percentiles, nearest rank. | `pdd_measured` |
| `mos_p10` | mos | Tenth-percentile MOS across dialogs holding a stream sipnab can score, worst stream per dialog. | `mos_grounded_dialogs` |
| `retransmit_rate` | retransmissions per dialog | `retransmits` over `dialogs`. Never refused — a group exists because a dialog fell into it. | `dialogs` |

How sipnab counts the metrics:

- **A seizure is an INVITE dialog that reached a final response.** A REGISTER
  is not a seizure, and neither is an INVITE still ringing when the capture
  ended.
- **Delivered means a 2xx or one of `480`, `486`, `487`, `600` and `603`**:
  the callee unavailable, busy, busy everywhere, declining, or the caller
  hanging up on a call that had already reached the far end. A trunk whose
  calls all end in `486` has an ASR of 0 and an NER of 100.
  `408 Request Timeout` does not count as delivered, because a proxy sends it
  both for a phone that did not answer and for a next hop it could not reach.
- **ACD times the conversation, not the dialog.** A call that rang for five
  seconds, talked for sixty and took one more on the BYE handshake contributes
  60 seconds.
- **Percentiles use nearest rank, with no interpolation**, so each percentile
  is a value an actual call had.
- **sipnab rounds every metric to two decimal places.** For the exact ratio,
  divide the two integers in `population`.
- **Groups rank by dialog count, largest first, ties broken by value.**
  `other_count` holds the number of dialogs in the groups past `top_n`, with
  no metrics. The groups plus `other_count` always equal `total_matched`.

**Three dimensions are available here and not in `aggregate_dialogs`.** Every
dimension `aggregate_dialogs` accepts is also accepted here:

| Dimension | Value | Fenced? |
|---|---|---|
| `to_domain` | The host half of the To URI, port stripped, IPv6 brackets kept. | Yes — the sender wrote it. |
| `hour` | The calendar hour the dialog opened in, aligned to the epoch like [`timeline`](#timeline) buckets, RFC 3339. | No |
| `next_hop` | `host:port` the opening message went to, read off the IP and transport headers. | No |

`to_domain`, `to.user`, `from.user` and `ua` values arrive wrapped in
`⟦untrusted-capture-data⟧`, because the sender wrote them (see [Untrusted
capture text](@/docs/mcp-protocol.md#untrusted-capture-text)). A state name, a
status code, an address, a codec and `next_hop` come back verbatim, because
sipnab derived them.

`next_hop` names the address and port the opening message went to, as seen at
the capture point. It names the actual next hop only when the capture point
sits beside the sender, as on a proxy capturing its own trunk traffic.

`by` takes one dimension. To break a group down further, call again with a
`filter` that selects that group. When a count alone answers the question, use
`aggregate_dialogs`, which skips the metric computation.


## Find — narrow to the calls that matter

You know something is wrong but not which call. These cut a capture down to the dialogs worth reading: by symptom, by text, by time, or by relationship to a call you already have.

### `search_by_time`

Returns dialogs whose first message falls in the window, oldest first.

| Name | Type | Legal values | If omitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | string | An inclusive RFC 3339 instant, such as `"2026-07-31T14:00:00Z"`. A malformed one fails with `start 'x' is not RFC 3339`. | Required — the call fails. |
| `end?` | string? | An exclusive RFC 3339 instant after `start`. At or before `start` fails with `invalid_params` (-32602). | Everything from `start` onward. |
| `filter?` | string? | An alias name or a raw [DSL](@/docs/filter-dsl.md) expression, ANDed with the window. | The window alone decides the page. |
| `limit?` | u32? | Ceiling is `--mcp-max-rows` (1000 by default). Higher clamps to it, `0` means the default. | 50 rows. |
| `cursor?` | string? | The previous response's `next_cursor`, verbatim (`<RFC 3339 created_at>\|<Call-ID>`). A malformed timestamp half fails with `invalid_params`. | Starts at the oldest dialog in the window. |
| `fields?` | string[]? | Field names to keep on each row, plus `call_id`. The row here is already narrow, so name one of the four below — see [Narrowing a row with `fields`](@/docs/mcp-tools.md#narrowing-a-row-with-fields). | The whole row. |
| `max_response_bytes?` | u64? | Bytes for the whole response. Ceiling is `--mcp-max-response-bytes` (1048576 unless the operator changed it). Higher clamps to it, `0` means the ceiling. Past it the page ends early at a whole row with `truncated_by: "bytes"` — see [Rules every tool follows](@/docs/mcp-tools.md#rules-every-tool-follows). | The ceiling. |

**Returns** `{ dialogs, returned, total_matched, truncated, truncated_by,
next_cursor, capture_identity, source_exhausted, source_stopped_early,
schema_version }`, with `truncated_by` present only when a bound cut the page.
Each row carries `call_id`, `created_at`, `state` and `final_status_code` —
**a narrower row than [`list_dialogs`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#list-dialogs) returns**, with no
`msg_count`, no `from_user`, no `timing` and no `frame`. No markers appear
here either, because none of those four fields is free text. Feed a `call_id` to another
tool when you need the rest.

`total_matched` counts every dialog in the window before `limit` applies, so a
small answer from a quiet window reads differently from a truncated one.

`filter` turns "failed calls between 14:00 and 14:05" into a single call. The
window narrows first and the filter runs over what survives.

The example runs against [`tests/pcap-samples/sipp-branch-scenario.pcapng`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/raw/main/tests/pcap-samples/sipp-branch-scenario.pcapng). The
same window without a filter answers `total_matched: 247`:

```jsonc
// search_by_time { "start": "2016-11-17T21:52:35Z", "end": "2016-11-17T21:53:00Z",
//                  "filter": "problems", "limit": 2 }
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "dialogs": [
    {
      "call_id": "call-10-synth@192.0.2.10",
      "created_at": "2016-11-17T21:52:36.203349+00:00",
      "final_status_code": 403,
      "state": "Failed"
    },
    {
      "call_id": "call-25-synth@192.0.2.10",
      "created_at": "2016-11-17T21:52:37.703349+00:00",
      "final_status_code": 403,
      "state": "Failed"
    }
  ],
  "returned": 2,
  "total_matched": 16,
  "truncated": true,
  "truncated_by": "rows",
  "next_cursor": "2016-11-17T21:52:37.703349Z|call-25-synth@192.0.2.10",
  "capture_identity": {
    "node": "capture-01",
    "instance": "128e5a18df0061de520f1d-2",
    "dialog_generation": 9015,
    "stream_generation": 0
  },
  "source_exhausted": true,
  "source_stopped_early": false
}
```

**To read the rest of a truncated window, pass `next_cursor` back** with the
same `start`, `end` and `filter`. `total_matched` counts the whole window, not
the remainder, so it stays the same as you page. The cursor is the same
compound form [`list_dialogs`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#list-dialogs) issues. Treat it
as opaque and pass it back exactly as it arrived.

### `validate_filter`

Compiles a Filter DSL expression, counts what it selects, and returns no rows.

Use it to build a filter for [`list_dialogs`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#list-dialogs),
[`find_problems`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#find-problems),
[`search_by_time`](#search-by-time),
[`aggregate_dialogs`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#aggregate-dialogs) or
[`group_dialogs`](#group-dialogs) without fetching a page of rows per attempt.
It also tells apart the two outcomes a list tool reports the same way: an
expression that does not parse, and an expression that parses but selects
nothing.

| Name | Type | Legal values | If omitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `expr` | string | A raw [filter DSL](@/docs/filter-dsl.md) expression, **or** one of the diagnostic aliases [`list_dialogs`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#list-dialogs) takes. Nothing you can put here fails the call. | Required — the call fails. |

**A parse failure is a successful call.** Other tools reject a bad filter
with `invalid_params`. This one answers `valid: false` with the parser's own
text in `error`, position, caret and hint included. It raises a JSON-RPC
error only for an internal failure.

```jsonc
// validate_filter { "expr": "state = Failed" }
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "expr": "state = Failed",
  "valid": false,
  "error": "invalid filter 'state = Failed': unexpected input at position 6: '='\n  state = Failed\n        ^\nvalid operators: ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=, =~ (regex)\nsee docs/filter-dsl.md for fields, values, and diagnostic aliases",
  "total_matched": null,
  "total_dialogs": 2,
  "capture_identity": { "node": "capture-01", "instance": "cc2cb18df0ea68adfb9c9-2",
                        "dialog_generation": 13, "stream_generation": 2 },
  "source_exhausted": true,
  "source_stopped_early": false
}
```

On a parse failure `total_matched` is `null`, not `0`. Once the expression
parses, `total_matched` counts every matching dialog in the store, with no
cursor and no truncation. The example runs against
[`tests/pcap-samples/sip-rtp-g711.pcap`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/raw/main/tests/pcap-samples/sip-rtp-g711.pcap):

```jsonc
// validate_filter { "expr": "state == 'Completed' and rtp.mos < 4.5" }
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "expr": "state == 'Completed' and rtp.mos < 4.5",
  "valid": true,
  "error": null,
  "total_matched": 1,
  "total_dialogs": 2,
  "capture_identity": { "node": "capture-01", "instance": "cc2cb18df0ea68adfb9c9-2",
                        "dialog_generation": 13, "stream_generation": 2 },
  "source_exhausted": true,
  "source_stopped_early": false
}
```

**Read `total_dialogs` beside `total_matched`.** It is the number of dialogs
in the store, returned even on a parse failure: 0 matches out of 0 dialogs is
an empty capture, and 0 out of 4000 is an expression that selects nothing.

Aliases expand here as they do in every other tool, and this tool uses the
same filter compiler, so `list_dialogs` accepts an expression that validates
here. The response carries no provenance note, because it contains
nothing read from the capture.

### `tail_dialogs`

Incremental fetch of the dialogs updated after a cursor position.

| Name | Type | Legal values | If omitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cursor?` | string? | The previous response's `next_cursor`, verbatim (`<RFC 3339>\|<Call-ID>`). A bare RFC 3339 timestamp also parses, and filters strictly after it. | Starts from the beginning of the store. |
| `limit?` | u32? | Ceiling is `--mcp-max-rows` (1000 by default). Higher clamps to it, `0` means the default. | 50 rows. |
| `fields?` | string[]? | Field names to keep on each row, plus `call_id`. Same rules as [`list_dialogs`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#list-dialogs) — see [Narrowing a row with `fields`](@/docs/mcp-tools.md#narrowing-a-row-with-fields). | The whole row. |
| `max_response_bytes?` | u64? | Bytes for the whole response. Ceiling is `--mcp-max-response-bytes` (1048576 unless the operator changed it). Higher clamps to it, `0` means the ceiling. Past it the page ends early at a whole row with `truncated_by: "bytes"` — see [Rules every tool follows](@/docs/mcp-tools.md#rules-every-tool-follows). | The ceiling. |

Returns `{ dialogs, next_cursor, source_exhausted, source_stopped_early,
capture_identity }`, where
`dialogs` holds the same summary rows [`list_dialogs`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#list-dialogs) returns,
fencing included. The page carries no `returned` or `total_matched`, because
the store can change between polls. Poll until `dialogs` comes back empty and
`source_exhausted` is `true`.

`truncated` and `truncated_by` appear only when the byte budget cut the page:
`truncated: true` and `truncated_by: "bytes"`. A tail page cut by `limit` says
nothing extra, because its `next_cursor` already names the last row returned
and the next poll continues from there either way.

`next_cursor` is compound — `<RFC 3339>|<Call-ID>` — not a bare
timestamp. Several dialogs can share an `updated_at`, and the pair resumes
exactly after the last row returned, so a page boundary neither skips nor
repeats a dialog.

Pass it back unmodified. A bare timestamp built from a dialog's `updated_at`
also works, but it selects only dialogs updated strictly after that instant,
so the next page can skip or repeat dialogs that share the timestamp, with no
error. `|` occurs in neither an RFC 3339 timestamp nor a valid Call-ID
([RFC 3261](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3261.html) `word`).

`source_exhausted` is `false` while more dialog updates can still
arrive and `true` once the capture source is fully drained — the end of
an `-I` pcap replay, or a live capture that has hit its
`--count`/`--duration`/`--autostop` stop condition. sipnab keeps
serving MCP after that, so this is the flag to poll to learn a replay
has finished: stop when it turns `true` instead of polling forever.

```jsonc
// tail_dialogs { "limit": 1 }
{
  "dialogs": [
    {
      "call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20",
      "state": "Completed",
      "method": "INVITE",
      "from_user": "⟦untrusted-capture-data⟧sipp⟦/untrusted-capture-data⟧",
      "to_user": "⟦untrusted-capture-data⟧test⟦/untrusted-capture-data⟧",
      "msg_count": 6,
      "final_status_code": 200,
      "duration_sec": 8.504,
      "created_at": "2016-11-26T14:52:59.666393+00:00",
      "updated_at": "2016-11-26T14:53:08.170676+00:00",
```

### `await_condition`

Waits until a filter selects at least one dialog, or until a deadline passes —
whichever happens first. Use it on a live capture instead of a
[`tail_dialogs`](#tail-dialogs) polling loop: one call covers the whole wait.

| Name | Type | Legal values | If omitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `filter` | string | A named alias or a filter DSL expression, exactly what [`list_dialogs`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#list-dialogs) accepts. [`validate_filter`](#validate-filter) checks one without waiting. | Required — the call fails. |
| `timeout_seconds?` | u32? | Ceiling is `--mcp-max-wait-seconds` (60 by default). Higher clamps to it and sets `timeout_clamped`. `0` means "look once and answer". | 30 seconds. |
| `poll_interval_ms?` | u32? | Floor is 100 ms. sipnab raises anything smaller and returns the effective value. | 500 ms. |

Returns `{ schema_version, filter, matched, stopped_because, dialogs, returned,
total_matched, truncated, elapsed_ms, timeout_seconds, timeout_clamped,
poll_interval_ms, polls, scans, source_exhausted, source_stopped_early,
capture_identity }`, where `dialogs` holds the
same summary rows [`list_dialogs`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#list-dialogs) returns, fencing included,
and is empty unless `matched` is `true`.

There is no page-size argument. The tool returns at most 50 rows, or
`--mcp-max-rows` when the operator set that lower. `total_matched` and
`truncated` say whether more dialogs matched. To page through every match,
call [`list_dialogs`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#list-dialogs) with the same `filter`.

**A deadline that passes is a successful call**, carrying `matched: false`,
not an error.

`stopped_because` names which of three endings this was. The two negative ones
tell you whether asking again can help:

| Value | `matched` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `condition_met` | `true` | The filter selected at least one dialog |
| `deadline` | `false` | The wait ran out. Not yet — asking again may still find it |
| `source_exhausted` | `false` | The capture source drained, so this capture cannot produce a match. The wait returns at once rather than running to the deadline |

The limits this tool applies:

- **Deadline without `timeout_seconds`: 30 seconds.**
- **Deadline ceiling: 60 seconds.** Change it with `--mcp-max-wait-seconds`
  on the server command line. sipnab clamps a request above the ceiling
  instead of refusing it, and the response says `timeout_clamped: true`.
- **Poll interval without `poll_interval_ms`: 500 ms.**
- **Poll interval floor: 100 ms.** sipnab raises a smaller request to 100, and
  the response carries the value used.

For example, `{ "filter": "state == Failed", "timeout_seconds": 100,
"poll_interval_ms": 10 }` against a server with the default ceiling answers
`"timeout_seconds": 60`, `"timeout_clamped": true` and
`"poll_interval_ms": 100`.

`polls` counts the looks and `scans` counts the looks that ran the filter. A
look at a capture that has not changed since the last one skips the filter, so
`scans` can be lower than `polls`.

A waiting call holds one of the `--mcp-max-concurrent` slots until it returns,
and nothing it allocates outlives it.

The example runs against
[`tests/pcap-samples/sip-problem-call.pcap`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/raw/main/tests/pcap-samples/sip-problem-call.pcap),
which holds four failed calls:


### `find_correlated`

Finds the other legs of one call — the far side of a B2BUA, SBC or PBX hop.

| Name | Type | Legal values | If omitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `call_id` | string | A Call-ID the store holds — the leg to correlate **from**. A Call-ID the store does not hold fails with a message such as `call_id 'nope@192.0.2.1' not found`. | Required — the call fails. |
| `limit?` | u32? | Ceiling is `--mcp-max-rows` (1000 by default). Higher clamps to it, `0` means the default. | 50 legs. |

Returns `source_call_id`, `legs`, `total_matched`, `heuristic_only`,
`capture_identity`, `timing_clock`, `source_exhausted`,
`source_stopped_early` and `schema_version`. An unknown `call_id` fails with
`invalid_params` (`call_id 'nope' not found`, `data.reason: "not_found"`), the
answer REST's `/correlated` route gives as 404 and `--correlate` as exit 1. A
call with no related legs answers with an empty `legs` array and
`total_matched: 0`, not an error. There
is no cursor: when `total_matched` is larger than the legs returned, raise
`limit`, up to `--mcp-max-rows`.

The example runs against
[`tests/pcap-samples/sip-rtp-g711.pcap`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/raw/main/tests/pcap-samples/sip-rtp-g711.pcap),
whose two calls share an SDP origin:

```jsonc
// find_correlated { "call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20" }
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "source_call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20",
  "legs": [
    { "call_id": "1-1968@10.0.2.20", "score": 90, "strategy": "sdp_origin",
      "identifier_match": true, "observed_gap_ms": null }
  ],
  "total_matched": 1,
  "heuristic_only": false,
  "capture_identity": {
    "node": "capture-01",
    "instance": "12cfb618df00766c6ccc3d-2",
    "dialog_generation": 13,
    "stream_generation": 2
  },
  "timing_clock": null,             // non-null only when a timing_heuristic leg is returned
  "source_exhausted": true,
  "source_stopped_early": false
}
```

**Read `strategy`, not just `score`.** Two strategies score 100 and they are not
the same claim:

| `strategy` | What it means | Survives a B2BUA? |
|---|---|---|
| `session_id` | [RFC 7989](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7989.html) `Session-ID` matched | **Yes, by design** |
| `x_call_id` | A configured header matched (none configured by default) | Only if the SBC inserts it |
| `charging_vector_related_icid` | One leg's [RFC 7315](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7315.html) `related-icid` names the other's `icid-value` | Yes — but only when the B2BUA chose to emit it (`MAY`) |
| `sdp_origin` | The [RFC 8866](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8866.html) SDP origin tuple matched | Only if the SBC forwards SDP untouched |
| `charging_vector_icid` | Both legs carry the same RFC 7315 `icid-value` | Not by design: an ICID identifies one dialog, and a B2BUA is two |
| `via_branch` | Two INVITEs shared a Via branch | No: a new transaction gets a new branch |
| `timing_heuristic` | Same endpoint, close in time | Not an identifier at all |

**The two `P-Charging-Vector` rows read one header in two ways.**
[RFC 7315 section 4.6](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7315.html#section-4.6)
says the ICID identifies *a dialog*, so a conformant B2BUA emits a different
`icid-value` on each side, and `charging_vector_icid` finds no match across
it. A `charging_vector_icid` match means an intermediary copied one dialog's
identifier onto a second dialog. The parameter that links the two sides of a
hop is `related-icid`
([RFC 7315 section 4.6.4.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7315.html#section-4.6.4.1)),
and it is optional.

Two limits apply to both:

- The first proxy generates the icid
  ([RFC 7315 section 5.6](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7315.html#section-5.6)), so a leg arriving from an endpoint carries none and this is useless at
  the access edge.
- [RFC 7315 section 4.6.2.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7315.html#section-4.6.2.2) lets the next hop *"modify the contents"*, which
  [RFC 7315 section 6.6](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7315.html#section-6.6) calls normal behavior, so unlike `Session-ID` there is no end-to-end
  constancy requirement at all.

The design record is
[`docs/design/icid-correlation.md`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/docs/design/icid-correlation.md).

Neither strategy puts the matched ICID in the response, because
[RFC 7315 section 4.6](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7315.html#section-4.6)'s
suggested construction embeds the generating proxy's hostname or address in
it.

`identifier_match` is `true` when the leg matched on a value both legs carry,
and `false` for `timing_heuristic`. `heuristic_only` is `true` when *every*
returned leg came from `timing_heuristic`: treat such a set of legs as a
hypothesis to confirm, not a finding.

`observed_gap_ms` carries a number **only** for `timing_heuristic` legs, and
`null` on an identifier match. Read it with the leg's score: a 15 ms gap and a
1,900 ms gap can score the same.

When the legs carry no correlation header, `timing_heuristic` is the only
strategy that can link them, and on a busy SBC unrelated calls can share an
endpoint inside its window.

### `get_call_tree`

Every leg of one call, as a tree.

Use it for a call that crosses an SBC, a PBX or a B2BUA, where one call is
several dialogs. [`find_correlated`](#find-correlated) answers one hop from one
Call-ID, and [`get_dialog`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#get-dialog) returns one leg.
`get_call_tree` follows the correlations from any leg and returns every leg it
reaches, the same set the TUI's extended call flow (the `x` key) shows.

| Name | Type | Legal values | If omitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `call_id` | string | Any leg of the call. The walk is symmetric, so naming the B-leg returns the same set rooted differently. A Call-ID the store does not hold fails with a message such as `call_id 'nope@192.0.2.1' not found`. | Required — the call fails. |
| `limit?` | u32? | Maximum legs including the root. Ceiling is `--mcp-max-rows` (1000 by default), higher clamps to it, `0` means the default. | 50 legs. |

The example runs against
[`tests/pcap-samples/sip-rtp-g711.pcap`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/raw/main/tests/pcap-samples/sip-rtp-g711.pcap),
whose two calls share an SDP origin, with each leg's `dialog` summary trimmed to
its first three keys:

```jsonc
// get_call_tree { "call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20" }
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "root_call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20",
  "legs": [
    {
      "call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20",
      "depth": 0,
      "parent_call_id": null,
      "score": null,
      "strategy": null,
      "identifier_match": null,
      "followed": true,
      "dialog": { "call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20", "state": "Completed", "method": "INVITE" }
    },
    {
      "call_id": "1-1968@10.0.2.20",
      "depth": 1,
      "parent_call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20",
      "score": 90,
      "strategy": "sdp_origin",
      "identifier_match": true,
      "followed": true,
      "dialog": { "call_id": "1-1968@10.0.2.20", "state": "InCall", "method": "INVITE" }
    }
  ],
  "total_legs": 2,
  "max_depth": 1,
  "truncated": false,
  "heuristic_edges": 0,
  "total_messages": 10,
  "first_activity": "2016-11-26T14:52:59.666393+00:00",
  "last_activity": "2016-11-26T14:53:08.290927+00:00",
  "capture_identity": { "node": "capture-01", "instance": "cc2cb18df0ea68adfb9c9-2",
                        "dialog_generation": 13, "stream_generation": 2 }
}
```

Every leg past the root names the leg it came from (`parent_call_id`), how far
out it sits (`depth`), and the strategy and score of that one edge — the same
`strategy` vocabulary [`find_correlated`](#find-correlated) tabulates. The root
carries `null` for all four, because the caller named it rather than any
strategy matching it.

**The walk does not expand `timing_heuristic` edges.** It follows the six
strategies that compare a value both legs carry. `timing_heuristic` links two
INVITE dialogs that share an endpoint address and started inside the
leg-correlation window, and on a busy proxy that links unrelated calls. A
timing edge still appears in `legs` with `followed: false`. To follow it, call
`get_call_tree` again rooted at that leg.

**Read `followed` before you read the shape.** A leg with `followed: false`
is one the walk did not expand: either a `timing_heuristic` edge, or a leg
still queued when `limit` stopped the walk. `truncated: true` says `limit`
stopped the walk.

`heuristic_edges` counts the guesses in the whole tree. Zero means every link is
an identifier both legs carried. `total_messages` is the size of the merged
ladder the TUI's extended flow renders, and `first_activity` and
`last_activity` bracket the call rather than the root leg.

An unknown `call_id` fails with `invalid_params` (`call_id 'nope' not found`,
`data.reason: "not_found"`). A dialog with no other legs comes back as a
one-leg tree with `total_legs: 1` and `max_depth: 0`.

### `compare_dialogs`

"Why did this one work and that one not?"

**Parameters:** `call_id_a` and `call_id_b` (both string, both required) — two
Call-IDs the store holds. Either one unknown fails with `invalid_params` naming
it. No optional parameters, and passing the same Call-ID twice is legal and
answers with an empty `differences`.

Each side reports `call_id`, `state`, `final_status_code`, `msg_count`,
`methods` (sorted) and `hints`. `differences` names the fields that differ, so
you are not diffing two objects by eye. The example compares the two calls in
[`tests/pcap-samples/sip-rtp-g711.pcap`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/raw/main/tests/pcap-samples/sip-rtp-g711.pcap):

```jsonc
// compare_dialogs { "call_id_a": "1-1966@10.0.2.20", "call_id_b": "1-1968@10.0.2.20" }
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "a": { "call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20", "state": "Completed", "final_status_code": 200,
         "msg_count": 6, "methods": ["ACK", "BYE", "INVITE"], "hints": [] },
  "b": { "call_id": "1-1968@10.0.2.20", "state": "InCall", "final_status_code": 200,
         "msg_count": 4, "methods": ["ACK", "INVITE"], "hints": [] },
  "differences": ["state", "msg_count", "methods"],
  "capture_identity": { "node": "capture-01", "instance": "cc2cb18df0ea68adfb9c9-2",
                        "dialog_generation": 13, "stream_generation": 2 }
}
```

`final_status_code` matches on both sides here and so stays out of
`differences` — the second call simply never sent a `BYE`.


## Diagnose one call

You have a call-id. These explain what happened to that one call -- its signaling, its media, and the specific negotiations that tend to break.

### `get_dialog_report`

Per-call diagnostic report for one Call-ID, with the same content as
`sipnab -N --call-report <Call-ID>`.

| Name | Type | Legal values | If omitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `call_id` | string | A Call-ID the store holds. An unknown one fails with `invalid_params` (-32602) naming the value. | Required — the call fails. |
| `format?` | string? | `"json"`, `"markdown"` or `"text"`. Anything else fails with `unknown format 'x', expected json\|markdown\|text`. | `"json"`. |

`"json"` answers with the structured object below. `"markdown"` and `"text"`
answer with one text block holding the rendered report, byte-identical to what
[`render_ladder`](#render-ladder) produces for the same dialog. All three append
the provenance note as a second content block. The two rendered formats also
carry the `INCOMPLETE RUN` block described under
[`get_capture_report`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#get-capture-report) when the capture was not read in
full. `"json"` carries `source_exhausted` and `source_stopped_early` as fields
instead, and `capture_identity`, which names the capture the report came from.

The example runs against [`tests/pcap-samples/sip-rtp-g711.pcap`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/raw/main/tests/pcap-samples/sip-rtp-g711.pcap):

```jsonc
// get_dialog_report { "call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20" }
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20",
  "state": "Completed",
  "method": "INVITE",
  "final_status_code": 200,
  "final_status_reason": "OK",
  "from": "sipp",
  "from_display": "PCMU/8000",
  "to": "test",
  "to_display": "test",
  "msg_count": 6,
  "duration_sec": 8.504,
  "frame": "tests/pcap-samples/sip-rtp-g711.pcap#0@db88659b94678546",
  "input_origin": "wire",
  "timing": {
    "retransmits": 0,
    "setup_ms": 4,
    "teardown_ms": 0,
    "trying_delay_ms": 0
  },
  "diagnosis": {
    "hints": [
      "RTP flowed 10.0.2.15:27942 -> 10.0.2.20:6000 only (SSRC 0x343da99b). No reverse media flow detected."
    ],
    "nat_mismatch": false,
    "no_media": false,
    "one_way_audio": true,
    "private_media_address": false
  },
  "termination": {
    "cause_code": 16,
    "cause_text": "NORMAL_CLEARING",
    "frame_ref": 4,
    "protocol": "Q.850",
    "source_header": "Reason"
  },
  "sdp_timeline": [ /* the same rows get_sdp_timeline returns */ ],
  "streams": [ /* the same rows rtp_stats returns, without mos */ ],
  "capture_identity": { "node": "capture-01", "instance": "cc2cb18df0ea68adfb9c9-2",
                        "dialog_generation": 13, "stream_generation": 2 },
  "source_exhausted": true,
  "source_stopped_early": false
}
```

`termination` says why the call ended, when a message on the wire named a
cause: here the `BYE` carries a `Reason` header with Q.850 cause 16. It is the
same object [`triage_call`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#triage-call) documents on the
core bundle page. When nothing on the wire named a cause, the key is absent,
not `null`.

This report bundles what [`triage_call`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#triage-call),
[`get_sdp_timeline`](#get-sdp-timeline) and [`rtp_stats`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#rtp-stats) answer
separately, so one call replaces three when you already know which call to read.
Its `streams` rows omit `mos` and `mos_grounded` — ask `rtp_stats` when the
question is audio quality rather than what the call did.

Unlike the summary rows elsewhere, `from` and `to` here arrive **unfenced**.
The trailing provenance note says which values in the report came from the
capture, so treat those as text the sender wrote.

### `get_message`

Single SIP message at a given zero-based index.

| Name | Type | Legal values | If omitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `call_id` | string | A Call-ID the store holds. | Required — the call fails. |
| `index` | u32 | `0` to `msg_count - 1` for that dialog. | Required — the call fails. |

**Where an index comes from,** because the number means nothing on its own:
`msg_count` on any [`list_dialogs`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#list-dialogs) row is the count, so the last
valid index is `msg_count - 1`. [`get_dialog`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#get-dialog) reports each page's
`first_index`, so the Nth row of that page sits at `first_index + N`, and every
[`lint_dialog`](#lint-dialog) finding reports the `message_index` it fired on.

An index at or past the end fails with `invalid_params`, and the message
carries the dialog's message count: `index 99 out of range for dialog with 6
messages`.

Returns one message in the same shape [`get_dialog`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#get-dialog) uses for a
`messages` row, plus the provenance note as a second content block. The
difference is the fencing: this tool wraps `from`, `to`, `contact`, `sdp`, `ua`,
`reason`, `malformed` and `extension_headers`, and leaves `call_id`, addresses,
ports, `method`, `status_code`, `cseq` and timestamps verbatim so they pass into
the next call.

```jsonc
// get_message { "call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20", "index": 0 }
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20",
  "method": "INVITE",
  "is_request": true,
  "cseq": { "method": "INVITE", "number": 1 },
  "from": "⟦untrusted-capture-data⟧\"PCMU/8000\" <sip:sipp@10.0.2.20:5060>;tag=1⟦/untrusted-capture-data⟧",
  "to": "⟦untrusted-capture-data⟧test <sip:test@10.0.2.15:5060>⟦/untrusted-capture-data⟧",
  "contact": "⟦untrusted-capture-data⟧sip:sipp@10.0.2.20:5060⟦/untrusted-capture-data⟧",
  "sdp": "⟦untrusted-capture-data⟧v=0\no=- 42 42 IN IP4 10.0.2.20\ns=-\nc=IN IP4 10.0.2.20\nt=0 0\nm=audio 6000 RTP/AVP 0\na=rtpmap:0 PCMU/8000\na=recvonly\n⟦/untrusted-capture-data⟧",
  "src": "10.0.2.20",
  "src_port": 5060,
  "dst": "10.0.2.15",
  "dst_port": 5060,
  "transport": "UDP",
  "timestamp": "2016-11-26T14:52:59.666393+00:00",
  "frame": "tests/pcap-samples/sip-rtp-g711.pcap#0@db88659b94678546",
  "dscp": 0,
  "input_origin": "wire",
  "extension_headers": [
    "⟦untrusted-capture-data⟧Via: SIP/2.0/UDP 10.0.2.20:5060;branch=z9hG4bK-1966-1-0⟦/untrusted-capture-data⟧",
    "⟦untrusted-capture-data⟧Max-Forwards: 70⟦/untrusted-capture-data⟧",
    "⟦untrusted-capture-data⟧Content-Type: application/sdp⟦/untrusted-capture-data⟧",
    "⟦untrusted-capture-data⟧Content-Length: 123⟦/untrusted-capture-data⟧"
  ],
  "capture_identity": { "node": "capture-01", "instance": "cc2cb18df0ea68adfb9c9-2",
                        "dialog_generation": 13, "stream_generation": 2 },
  "source_exhausted": true,
  "source_stopped_early": false
}
```

`dscp` and `input_origin` carry the meanings [`get_dialog`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#get-dialog) gives
them. sipnab omits either key rather than sending `null` when it observed
neither.

#### `extension_headers`

Every header the fields above do NOT already carry, in wire form
(`"Name: value"`) and in wire order — one entry per header line.

Read it for vendor-, carrier- and SBC-specific headers that have no named
field: `X-Asterisk-*`, `Reason`, `Diversion`, `P-Asserted-Identity`,
`Remote-Party-ID`, `Require`, `RSeq`.

Six header names never appear here, because they are already fields of their
own: `Call-ID`, `From`, `To`, `Contact`, `User-Agent` and `CSeq`. The list
holds every other header line, `Via` and `Content-Length` included.

**The list keeps duplicates and wire order.** `Via` is a stack whose order is
the route the request took, so three `Via` lines are three entries in the order
they arrived.

**Fenced whole, name included.** The sender chose the header name as well as
the value, so the marker pair wraps the entire `Name: value` string. The
threat model for this text is in
[deferred-and-declined.md](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/docs/design/deferred-and-declined.md#the-prompt-injection-chain-grounded).

The list has the parser's bounds: sipnab refuses a message with more than 200
headers or a header line longer than 8 KiB.

### `render_ladder`

Call-flow ladder for one Call-ID.

| Name | Type | Legal values | If omitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `call_id` | string | A Call-ID the store holds. | Required — the call fails. |
| `format?` | string? | `"markdown"`, `"text"` or `"mermaid"`. Anything else, `"json"` included, fails with `unknown format 'x', expected markdown\|text\|mermaid`. | `"markdown"`. |

Returns one text content block holding the rendered report, and the provenance
note as a second block.

`"mermaid"` returns a Mermaid `sequenceDiagram` of the call instead, fenced as
untrusted text. Each arrow carries a `Note` with what the ladder knows about
that message: its offset from the first message (`+0.500s`), `PDD <n>ms` on
the first 180, the SDP change against the call's previous SDP (`+G722`,
`−PCMU`, `HOLD`, `UNHOLD`) and `retransmission`. IPv6 endpoints carry brackets
(`[2001:db8::1]:5060`). The browser analyzer draws the same rows, and the SDP
change badges match the TUI ladder's. There is no JSON shape here — ask
[`get_dialog_report`](#get-dialog-report) with `format: "json"` for fields a
program can read.

```jsonc
render_ladder { "call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20" }
```

To get the same report from the command line, add `--no-cli-print`, which
leaves out the per-message dump the CLI otherwise writes first:

```bash
sipnab -N -I tests/pcap-samples/sip-rtp-g711.pcap --call-report 1-1966@10.0.2.20 --markdown --no-cli-print
```

Over a capture that was not read in full — still loading, or a read that
stopped before the file's end — the tool appends an `INCOMPLETE RUN` block
after the ladder, which `--call-report` does not. The block does not change
the ladder above it.

```text
# Call Report: 1-1966@10.0.2.20

## Summary

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Time | 2016-11-26 14:52:59 -> 14:53:08 (8s) |
| From | sipp |
| To | test |
| State | Completed |
| Cause | Q.850 cause 16 "NORMAL_CLEARING" [Reason] |

## Timing

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| PDD | - |
| Setup | 0.00s |
| Ring | - |
| Teardown | 0.00s |
| Retransmits | 0 |

## Media Streams

| SSRC | Codec | Source | Destination | Packets | Jitter | Loss | MOS | MOS_CQEW |
|------|-------|--------|-------------|---------|--------|------|-----|----------|
| 0x343da99b | PCMU | 10.0.2.15:27942 | 10.0.2.20:6000 | 425 | 0ms | 0.0% | 4.36 | - |

## Issues

- RTP flowed 10.0.2.15:27942 -> 10.0.2.20:6000 only (SSRC 0x343da99b). No reverse media flow detected.
```

### `get_sdp_timeline`

The offer/answer exchanges in order — codecs, media address, port and mode per
negotiation, including re-INVITEs. Use it when audio changed mid-call, or when
the two ends disagree about the codec.

**Parameters:** `call_id` (string, required) — a Call-ID the store holds. No
optional parameters.

Every exchange carries `direction` (`offer` or `answer`), `codecs`,
`media_addr`, `media_port`, `mode` (`sendrecv`, `sendonly`, `recvonly` or
`inactive`), `timestamp`, and `event` — `null` unless sipnab classified the
exchange, as with the `MediaAnchorChange` below. A call carrying no SDP answers
with an empty `exchanges` array rather than an error.

```jsonc
// get_sdp_timeline { "call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20" }
{
  "call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20",
  "capture_identity": { "node": "capture-01", "instance": "cc2cb18df0ea68adfb9c9-2",
                        "dialog_generation": 13, "stream_generation": 2 },
  "exchanges": [
    {
      "codecs": [
        "PCMU"
      ],
      "direction": "offer",
      "event": null,
      "media_addr": "10.0.2.20",
      "media_port": 6000,
      "mode": "recvonly",
      "timestamp": "2016-11-26T14:52:59.666393+00:00"
    },
    {
      "codecs": [
        "PCMU",
        "telephone-event"
      ],
      "direction": "answer",
      "event": "MediaAnchorChange",
      "media_addr": "10.0.2.15",
      "media_port": 27942,
      "mode": "sendonly",
      "timestamp": "2016-11-26T14:52:59.670743+00:00"
    }
  ],
  "schema_version": 1
}
```

The offer promises `recvonly` on `10.0.2.20:6000` and the answer replies
`sendonly` from `10.0.2.15:27942`, which is why
[`triage_call`](@/docs/mcp-tools-core.md#triage-call) calls this capture one-way media rather than a
fault.

### `check_codec_negotiation`

For `488 Not Acceptable Here`, which usually means nobody offered the far end a
codec it accepts.

**Parameters:** `call_id` (string, required) — a Call-ID the store holds. No
optional parameters.

Returns `offered`, `answered`, `common`, `result`, `sdp_exchange_count`,
`final_status_code`, `call_id`, `capture_identity`, `source_exhausted`,
`source_stopped_early` and `schema_version`. Each codec name in `offered`, `answered` and `common`
arrives fenced, because the sender wrote it in the SDP.

```jsonc
// check_codec_negotiation { "call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20" }
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20",
  "offered": ["⟦untrusted-capture-data⟧PCMU⟦/untrusted-capture-data⟧"],
  "answered": ["⟦untrusted-capture-data⟧PCMU⟦/untrusted-capture-data⟧",
               "⟦untrusted-capture-data⟧telephone-event⟦/untrusted-capture-data⟧"],
  "common": ["⟦untrusted-capture-data⟧PCMU⟦/untrusted-capture-data⟧"],
  "result": "ok",
  "final_status_code": 200,
  "sdp_exchange_count": 2,
  "capture_identity": { "node": "capture-01", "instance": "cc2cb18df0ea68adfb9c9-2",
                        "dialog_generation": 13, "stream_generation": 2 },
  "source_exhausted": true,
  "source_stopped_early": false
}
```

`result` has five values:

| Result | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | The two sides agreed | Codecs are not your problem |
| `no_common_codec` | Both offered codecs, none shared | A codec policy problem — compare the lists |
| `no_answer` | An offer went out, nothing came back | The call did not get far enough to negotiate |
| `sdp_present_but_no_codecs` | Both sides exchanged SDP, but neither listed a codec | Look at the SDP itself — a malformed or media-less `m=` line |
| `no_sdp_in_capture` | No SDP at all | Not a codec problem. Hold with inactive media, or a reject before any offer |

`no_answer` means the capture holds an SDP offer and no answer to it.
`no_sdp_in_capture` means the capture holds no SDP offer, so there is no
answer to look for.


## Conformance and rules

Whether the traffic obeys the RFCs, and which clause it broke. These turn "the call failed" into "12.1.1 requires a Contact and there is none".

### `lint_dialog`

Checks one call against the RFCs. Use it when the question is whether the
traffic obeys the specification. Use `triage_call` when the question is why a
call failed. A call can complete over messages that break four MUSTs, and a
fully conformant call can end busy.

The observation rules (`OBS-`) compare what the SDP declared with the media the
capture holds. They report, for example, that the SDP declared PCMU on payload
type 0 while the wire carried payload type 8, that RTP arrived on a port no
`m=` line advertised, that `sendrecv` promised media in both directions and
the capture holds it in one, or that the packet spacing contradicts
`a=ptime`.

The RFC 3261 syntax rules and the [RFC 3264](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3264.html) offer/answer rules run alongside
them. Everything citing [RFC 4566](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4566.html), 3551 or 5761 belongs to the observation half.
[SIP conformance rules](@/docs/sip-lint-rules.md) lists every rule, the section behind
it, and the suppression syntax.

| Name | Type | Legal values | If omitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `call_id` | string | A Call-ID the store holds. | Required — the call fails. |
| `rulesets?` | string[]? | The 16 selectors below, OR-ed together. An unknown one fails with `invalid_params` listing all 16. | The whole catalog, reported back as `rulesets: ["all"]`. |
| `severity_min?` | string? | `info`, `notice`, `warning` or `error`. Anything else fails with `unknown severity 'x'. Valid values: info, notice, warning, error`. | `info`, so the floor drops nothing. |
| `suppression_file?` | string? | A bare filename inside `--mcp-file-root`. A file sipnab cannot open fails with `invalid_params` rather than linting with every rule on. | sipnab walks for a `.sipnablint` beside the capture and upward to the project root. |

Selectors take two forms — the catalog's own names, and one per RFC the rules
cite:

- **By category:** `all`, `must`, `rfc` (MUST and SHOULD together), `interop`,
  `observation` (`observed` also works) and `syntax`.
- **By RFC:** `rfc3261`, `rfc3262`, `rfc3264`, `rfc3551`, `rfc4028`, `rfc4566`,
  `rfc5761`, `rfc7587`, `rfc7989`.

An unknown selector fails with `invalid_params` (-32602) naming the whole
vocabulary:

```text
unknown ruleset 'rfc3621'. Valid selectors: all, must, rfc, interop, observation, syntax, observed, rfc3261, rfc3262, rfc3264, rfc3551, rfc4028, rfc4566, rfc5761, rfc7587, rfc7989
```

Passing an empty array behaves as omitting the parameter.

The example runs against [`tests/pcap-samples/b2bua-asterisk.pcapng`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/raw/main/tests/pcap-samples/b2bua-asterisk.pcapng). Its SDP
negotiates `sendrecv` in both directions, and the capture carries 355 RTP
packets in one:

```jsonc
// lint_dialog { "call_id": "b2bua-leg-synth@203.0.113.101:5060",
//               "rulesets": ["observed"] }
{
  "call_id": "b2bua-leg-synth@203.0.113.101:5060",
  "capture_identity": {
    "dialog_generation": 64,
    "instance": "7771d18dfa97985500250-2",
    "node": "capture-01",
    "stream_generation": 2
  },
  "finding_count": 1,
  "findings": [
    {
      "basis": "observation",
      "expected": "media in both directions, as a=sendrecv promised",
      "explanation": "§6.1 makes sendrecv a promise to send as well as receive. One endpoint kept it and the other did not, which the far end hears as dead air on an answered call. The usual causes are a NAT with no inbound pinhole, a firewall dropping the return path, and an endpoint that answered sendrecv while muting locally.",
      "frame_ref": "tests/pcap-samples/b2bua-asterisk.pcapng#23@08cb2267de5498ce",
      "message_index": 0,
      "observed": "⟦untrusted-capture-data⟧355 RTP packets observed, none of them toward one negotiated endpoint⟦/untrusted-capture-data⟧",
      "rfc": 3264,
      "rule_id": "OBS-3264-6.1-DIRECTION-UNMET",
      "section": "6.1",
      "severity": "warning"
    }
  ],
  "findings_withheld": {
    "below_severity": 0,
    "capped": 0,
    "suppressed": 0
  },
  "message_count": 15,
  "rtp_streams_observed": 1,
  "rule_catalog": "docs/sip-lint-rules.md",
  "rules_not_evaluated": [
    {
      "reason": "needs the endpoint pairs RTCP arrived on. The stream store folds RTCP into the stream it reports on and keeps no record of where it landed, so no MCP tool can raise this rule.",
      "rule_ids": [
        "OBS-5761-5.1.1-RTCP-MUX-UNANSWERED"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "rulesets": [
    "observed"
  ],
  "schema_version": 1,
  "severity_counts": {
    "error": 0,
    "info": 0,
    "notice": 0,
    "warning": 1
  },
  "severity_min": "info",
  "source_exhausted": true,
  "source_stopped_early": false,
  "suppressions": {
    "file": null,
    "findings_suppressed": 0,
    "patterns": []
  }
}
```

To use a finding:

- **Cite `rfc` and `section`** rather than the prose of `explanation`, for
  example [RFC 3264 section 6.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3264.html#section-6.1).
  [`explain_rule`](#explain-rule) turns a `rule_id` back into the citation and
  the link.
- **Pass `frame_ref` to [`show_evidence`](@/docs/mcp-tools-captures.md#show-evidence)**
  to read the bytes of the frame the rule fired on.
- **Treat `observed` as capture text.** It quotes the capture and arrives
  fenced. `expected` and `explanation` are sipnab's own words and arrive
  unfenced.

`rules_not_evaluated` names the rules that did not run, grouped by reason, so
an empty `findings` list is not read as a pass for those rules. Two reasons
appear on this tool:

- No RTP reached the call, so the `OBS-` rules had nothing to compare the
  declaration against.
- `OBS-5761-5.1.1-RTCP-MUX-UNANSWERED` needs the endpoint pairs RTCP arrived
  on, which the MCP server does not record, so no MCP tool raises this rule.

#### Suppression, and what it must tell you

A project silences rules with a `.sipnablint` — one identifier per line, or a
prefix ending `*`, with `#` starting a comment. [SIP conformance
rules](@/docs/sip-lint-rules.md) documents the pattern syntax.

sipnab looks for one beside the capture, then climbs toward the project root
and stops there. A capture that sits outside any project — a corpus mount, a
share, `/tmp` — uses only a `.sipnablint` in its own directory.
`suppression_file` replaces the search, and a file it names that sipnab cannot
open fails with `invalid_params` instead of linting with every rule on.

Two response fields report what suppression and filtering left out. Every
call includes both, even when every number is zero:

```jsonc
"suppressions": {
  "file": "/srv/captures/.sipnablint",   // null when none applied
  "patterns": ["OBS-*", "SIP-3261-8.1.1.6-MAX-FORWARDS-MISSING"],
  "findings_suppressed": 4
},
"findings_withheld": { "suppressed": 4, "below_severity": 2, "capped": 0 }
```

Each count points at a different cause:

- **`suppressed`**: a pattern in the `.sipnablint` file that
  `suppressions.file` names. Edit that file, or pass another
  `suppression_file`.
- **`below_severity`**: your `severity_min`. Lower it to see them.
- **`capped`**: the per-rule cap of 25 findings.

`suppressed` and `below_severity` are exact counts. `capped` is a lower bound,
because a rule can stop evaluating once it reaches the cap.

### `validate_message`

Runs the same rules against one message, named by its zero-based index. Use it
to confirm a finding on one message, for example in a CI job or when
discussing one header with a vendor. `lint_dialog` reports `message_index` on
every finding, which is the index this tool takes.

| Name | Type | Legal values | If omitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `call_id` | string | A Call-ID the store holds. | Required — the call fails. |
| `index` | u32 | `0` to `msg_count - 1`. Out of range fails with `invalid_params` (-32602) naming the message count. | Required — the call fails. |
| `suppression_file?` | string? | A bare filename inside `--mcp-file-root`, exactly as [`lint_dialog`](#lint-dialog) takes it. Wins outright over the discovery walk. | sipnab walks for a `.sipnablint` beside the capture and upward. |

There is no `rulesets` or `severity_min` here. Every rule that can run on one
message runs, and the response reports the rest under `rules_not_evaluated`.

```jsonc
// validate_message { "call_id": "options-ping-c-synth@198.51.100.206", "index": 0 }
{
  "call_id": "options-ping-c-synth@198.51.100.206",
  "capture_identity": {
    "dialog_generation": 14,
    "instance": "77d2718dfa97b81aa9e86-2",
    "node": "capture-01",
    "stream_generation": 0
  },
  "finding_count": 2,
  "findings": [
    {
      "basis": "must",
      "expected": "Max-Forwards: 70",
      "explanation": "§8.1.1.6 makes a UAC insert one into every request it originates. Without it a routing loop has nothing to stop it, and RFC 3261 §16.6 leaves each proxy to invent its own starting value.",
      "frame_ref": "tests/pcap-samples/sip-488-codec-reject.pcapng#4@b2b8ff6b3eeddf54",
      "message_index": 0,
      "observed": "⟦untrusted-capture-data⟧no Max-Forwards header field⟦/untrusted-capture-data⟧",
      "rfc": 3261,
      "rule_id": "SIP-3261-8.1.1.6-MAX-FORWARDS-MISSING",
      "section": "8.1.1.6",
      "severity": "warning"
    },
    {
      "basis": "must",
      "expected": "branch=z9hG4bK...",
      "explanation": "§8.1.1.7 makes every compliant branch begin with z9hG4bK, so its absence identifies a stack predating RFC 3261 in one field. Transaction matching then falls back to the RFC 2543 rules, and CANCEL and ACK correlation stop being reliable.",
      "frame_ref": "tests/pcap-samples/sip-488-codec-reject.pcapng#4@b2b8ff6b3eeddf54",
      "message_index": 0,
      "observed": "⟦untrusted-capture-data⟧top Via branch without the z9hG4bK prefix⟦/untrusted-capture-data⟧",
      "rfc": 3261,
      "rule_id": "SIP-3261-8.1.1.7-BRANCH-COOKIE",
      "section": "8.1.1.7",
      "severity": "warning"
    }
  ],
  "findings_withheld": {
    "below_severity": 0,
    "capped": 0,
    "suppressed": 0
  },
  "message_count": 2,
  "message_index": 0,
  "rule_catalog": "docs/sip-lint-rules.md",
  "rules_not_evaluated": [
    {
      "reason": "reads a dialog's messages against each other, and this tool reads one message alone. Call lint_dialog.",
      "rule_ids": [
        "SIP-3261-8.1.1.2-TO-TAG-IN-INITIAL-REQUEST",
        "SIP-3261-17.1.1.3-ACK-CSEQ-MISMATCH",
        "SIP-3261-17.1.1.3-ACK-BRANCH-MISMATCH",
        "SIP-3261-12.1.1-RECORD-ROUTE-NOT-COPIED",
        "SIP-3262-4-PRACK-MISSING",
        "SDP-3264-6.1-ANSWER-NO-COMMON-FORMAT",
        "SDP-3264-6.1-ANSWER-EXTRA-FORMAT",
        "SDP-3264-6.1-ANSWER-DIRECTION-ILLEGAL",
        "SDP-3264-8.4-HOLD-CONNECTION-ZERO",
        "SDP-3264-8.3.2-DYNAMIC-PT-REBOUND",
        "SDP-3264-7-TELEPHONE-EVENT-ONE-WAY",
        "SDP-3264-8.2-REJECTED-STREAM-ATTRIBUTES",
        "SDP-7587-7-OPUS-RTPMAP-RATE"
      ]
    },
    {
      "reason": "compares the declaration against the observed media, and this tool reads one message alone. Call lint_dialog.",
      "rule_ids": [
        "OBS-3264-6.1-PT-UNDECLARED",
        "OBS-4566-5.14-MEDIA-PORT-MISMATCH",
        "OBS-3264-6.1-DIRECTION-UNMET",
        "OBS-4566-6-PTIME-MISMATCH",

    {
      "reason": "needs the endpoint pairs RTCP arrived on. The stream store folds RTCP into the stream it reports on and keeps no record of where it landed, so no MCP tool can raise this rule.",
      "rule_ids": [
        "OBS-5761-5.1.1-RTCP-MUX-UNANSWERED"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "schema_version": 1,
  "severity_counts": {
    "error": 0,
    "info": 0,
    "notice": 0,
    "warning": 2
  },
  "source_exhausted": true,
  "source_stopped_early": false,
  "suppressions": {
    "file": null,
    "findings_suppressed": 0,
    "patterns": []
  }
}
```

That example runs against [`tests/pcap-samples/sip-488-codec-reject.pcapng`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/raw/main/tests/pcap-samples/sip-488-codec-reject.pcapng),
whose first `OPTIONS` ping carries neither a `Max-Forwards` header field nor
the RFC 3261 branch cookie.

`observed` quotes the message, so it arrives fenced. `expected` is sipnab's own
words, so it does not. `frame_ref` points at the frame the finding fired on — hand
it to [`show_evidence`](@/docs/mcp-tools-captures.md#show-evidence) to read the bytes behind the claim.
`findings_withheld` counts what the response left out and why, and
`suppressions` names the `.sipnablint` file that took part, both of them exactly
as [`lint_dialog`](#lint-dialog) reports them.

Nineteen of the forty-one rules skip on a one-message run, and
`rules_not_evaluated` names them. Run `lint_dialog` first, and use this tool to
confirm one message.

### `explain_rule`

Returns the catalog entry for a rule identifier taken from a finding, a CI log
or a suppression file.

**Parameters:** `rule_id` (string, required) — one of the 41 catalog
identifiers, matched exactly, such as `OBS-3264-6.1-PT-UNDECLARED`. No optional
parameters, and the tool reads no capture, so it answers the same on any
server. An unknown identifier fails with `invalid_params` (-32602) **listing all
41**, so a call with any unknown identifier lists the catalog:

```text
'NOPE' is not a rule in the catalog. The 41 rules are: SIP-3261-8.1.1-MANDATORY-HEADER-MISSING, SIP-3261-20.16-CSEQ-MALFORMED, SIP-3261-20.14-CONTENT-LENGTH-MISMATCH, SIP-3261-25.1-HEADER-CONTROL-BYTE, SIP-3261-20-URI-BRACKETS, SIP-3261-19.1.1-URI-PARAM-DEMOTED, SIP-3261-8.1.1.6-MAX-FORWARDS-MISSING, SIP-3261-20.22-MAX-FORWARDS-RANGE, SIP-3261-8.1.1.7-BRANCH-COOKIE, SIP-3261-8.1.1.2-TO-TAG-IN-INITIAL-REQUEST, SIP-3261-8.1.1.5-CSEQ-METHOD-MISMATCH, SIP-3261-17.1.1.3-ACK-CSEQ-MISMATCH, SIP-3261-17.1.1.3-ACK-BRANCH-MISMATCH, SIP-3261-12.1.1-CONTACT-MISSING-IN-2XX, SIP-3261-12.1.1-RECORD-ROUTE-NOT-COPIED, SIP-3261-16.6-RECORD-ROUTE-NOT-LOOSE, SIP-3261-8.1.1.7-VIA-BRANCH-DUPLICATE, SIP-3261-7.3.1-SINGULAR-HEADER-REPEATED, SIP-3262-3-RELIABLE-PROVISIONAL-WITHOUT-RSEQ, SIP-3262-4-PRACK-MISSING, SIP-4028-7.1-SESSION-EXPIRES-BELOW-MIN-SE, SIP-4028-4-SESSION-EXPIRES-TOO-SMALL, SIP-4028-5-MIN-SE-TOO-SMALL, SIP-4028-9-REFRESHER-MISSING, SIP-7989-5-SESSION-ID-MALFORMED, SIP-7989-5-SESSION-ID-UPPERCASE, SIP-7989-11-SESSION-ID-LEGACY-FORM, SDP-3264-6.1-ANSWER-NO-COMMON-FORMAT, SDP-3264-6.1-ANSWER-EXTRA-FORMAT, SDP-3264-6.1-ANSWER-DIRECTION-ILLEGAL, SDP-3264-8.4-HOLD-CONNECTION-ZERO, SDP-3264-8.3.2-DYNAMIC-PT-REBOUND, SDP-3264-7-TELEPHONE-EVENT-ONE-WAY, SDP-3264-8.2-REJECTED-STREAM-ATTRIBUTES, SDP-7587-7-OPUS-RTPMAP-RATE, OBS-3264-6.1-PT-UNDECLARED, OBS-4566-5.14-MEDIA-PORT-MISMATCH, OBS-3264-6.1-DIRECTION-UNMET, OBS-4566-6-PTIME-MISMATCH, OBS-5761-5.1.1-RTCP-MUX-UNANSWERED, OBS-3551-4.2-FRAME-SIZE-IMPOSSIBLE
```

```jsonc
// explain_rule { "rule_id": "OBS-3264-6.1-DIRECTION-UNMET" }
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "rule_id": "OBS-3264-6.1-DIRECTION-UNMET",
  "title": "sendrecv negotiated, media observed one way",
  "severity": "warning",
  "basis": "observation",
  "rfc": 3264,
  "section": "6.1",
  "citation": "RFC 3264 §6.1",
  "url": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3264.html#section-6.1",
  "scope": "media",
  "rulesets": ["all", "observation", "observed", "rfc3264"],
  "rule_catalog": "docs/sip-lint-rules.md"
}
```

`rulesets` lists every selector that reaches this rule, so any entry passes
straight back as a `lint_dialog` `rulesets` value. `scope` says what the rule
has to read before it can run: `message`, `dialog` or `media`.

### `explain_response_code`

The meaning and class of a SIP status code, from the IANA registry.

**Parameters:** `code` (integer, required) — a SIP status code from 100 to 699.
Outside that range fails with `999 is not a SIP response code (100-699)`. No
optional parameters, and this tool reads no capture either, so it answers on a
server holding nothing.

```jsonc
// explain_response_code { "code": 488 }
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "code": 488,
  "class": "failure",     // provisional|success|redirect|challenge|canceled|declined|failure
  "explanation": "488 Not Acceptable Here — Codec negotiation failed. Compare the SDP offer against the callee's supported codecs and ptime values.",
  "registered": true
}
```

`class` distinguishes a challenge from a failure: `401` is `challenge`, not
`failure`, because a challenged request is waiting for credentials, not
refused. `registered: false` means the code is not in the IANA registry, as
with a vendor extension, and the response gives no meaning for it.


## Export and handoff

Getting the result out of sipnab and into the next tool, the next team, or a bug report someone else can reproduce.

### `generate_repro`

A SIPp scenario that replays one call, built around your hypothesis of the
cause.

`pin` names the aspects of the captured request you believe caused the
outcome, and the scenario copies them byte-for-byte. `vary` names the identity
fields SIPp regenerates per run, so the replay is a new call rather than a
retransmission of the captured one. Running the scenario then tests the
pinned aspects.

| Name | Type | Legal values | If omitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `call_id` | string | A Call-ID the store holds, carrying at least one request. | Required — the call fails. |
| `format?` | string? | `"sipp"`, the only one. Anything else fails with `unknown format 'x'; 'sipp' is the only one`. | `"sipp"`. |
| `pin?` | string[]? | Any of `branch`, `call_id`, `cseq`, `headers`, `request_uri`, `sdp`, `tags`, `user_agent`. An explicit `[]` means "nothing", not "the default". | Nothing pinned — the scenario tests no theory and the response says so. |
| `vary?` | string[]? | `branch`, `call_id`, `tags` — the three SIPp can regenerate. Anything else from the `pin` vocabulary fails, naming the three. | All three. |
| `filename?` | string? | A bare name in `--mcp-file-root` to write the scenario to as well. The text comes back either way. | The response carries the scenario and nothing touches the disk. |

```jsonc
// generate_repro { "call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20", "pin": ["sdp", "user_agent"] }
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20",
  "format": "sipp",
  "hypothesis": {
    "pinned": ["sdp", "user_agent"],
    "varied": ["branch", "call_id", "tags"],
    "generated": ["contact", "content_length", "cseq", "max_forwards", "request_uri", "via"],
    "omitted": ["headers"]
  },
  "asserted": { "provisional": [100], "final": 200 },
  "scenario": "<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\" ?>\n<!DOCTYPE scenario SYSTEM \"sipp.dtd\">\n<!-- Generated by sipnab from Call-ID 1-1966@10.0.2.20 -->\n<!-- pinned: sdp user_agent | varied: branch call_id tags -->\n<scenario name=\"sipnab repro 1-1966@10.0.2.20\">\n  <send retrans=\"500\">\n    <![CDATA[\n\nINVITE sip:test@[remote_ip]:[remote_port] SIP/2.0\nVia: SIP/2.0/[transport] [local_ip]:[local_port];branch=[branch]\nFrom: <sip:sipp@[local_ip]:[local_port]>;tag=[pid]SIPpTag00[call_number]\nTo: <sip:test@[remote_ip]:[remote_port]>\nCall-ID: [call_id]\nCSeq: 1 INVITE\nContact: <sip:sipp@[local_ip]:[local_port];transport=[transport]>\nMax-Forwards: 70\nContent-Type: application/sdp\nContent-Length: [len]\n\nv=0\no=- 42 42 IN IP4 10.0.2.20\ns=-\nc=IN IP4 10.0.2.20\nt=0 0\nm=audio 6000 RTP/AVP 0\na=rtpmap:0 PCMU/8000\na=recvonly\n\n    ]]>\n  </send>\n  <recv response=\"100\" optional=\"true\"/>\n  <recv response=\"200\"/>\n  <send>\n    <![CDATA[\n\nACK sip:test@[remote_ip]:[remote_port] SIP/2.0\nVia: SIP/2.0/[transport] [local_ip]:[local_port];branch=[branch]\n[last_From:]\n[last_To:]\n[last_Call-ID:]\nCSeq: 1 ACK\nContact: <sip:sipp@[local_ip]:[local_port];transport=[transport]>\nMax-Forwards: 70\nContent-Length: 0\n\n\n    ]]>\n  </send>\n  <pause milliseconds=\"2000\"/>\n  <send retrans=\"500\">\n    <![CDATA[\n\nBYE sip:test@[remote_ip]:[remote_port] SIP/2.0\nVia: SIP/2.0/[transport] [local_ip]:[local_port];branch=[branch]\n[last_From:]\n[last_To:]\n[last_Call-ID:]\nCSeq: 2 BYE\nMax-Forwards: 70\nContent-Length: 0\n\n\n    ]]>\n  </send>\n  <recv response=\"200\"/>\n</scenario>\n",
  "run": "sipp -sf <scenario.xml> -m 1 <proxy-host>:<port>",
  "caveats": [
    "user_agent was pinned and the captured request carries no User-Agent header, so none is sent",
    "the pinned body names the media endpoint the ORIGINAL caller advertised, so any RTP the far end sends goes there and not to the machine running SIPp",
    "SIPp sends from the host you run it on. Source address, routing and any IP access list differ from the capture, and a reproduction depends on those matching."
  ],
  "source_exhausted": true,
  "source_stopped_early": false
}
```

**Read the `hypothesis` block as a four-way split of the original request.**
`pinned` came across byte-for-byte, `varied` is what SIPp regenerates,
`generated` is what the template supplies instead of the capture, and `omitted`
is what the capture held and the scenario leaves out. Nothing falls outside
those four.

**Only `branch`, `call_id` and `tags` can vary**, because those are the fields
SIPp generates fresh for every call it places. Asking to vary anything else
fails:

```jsonc
{ "code": -32602,
  "message": "'sdp' cannot be varied: SIPp has no generator for it. Variable aspects are branch, call_id, tags. Pin it instead if it is part of your hypothesis." }
```

**An aspect in both `pin` and `vary` fails:**

```jsonc
{ "code": -32602,
  "message": "'call_id' is in both pin and vary. Held fixed and regenerated are opposite instructions, and a scenario that silently picked one would encode a theory nobody stated." }
```

All three identity fields vary by default. Pin them only when you intend the
replay to reach the proxy as a retransmission of the captured call.

**Anything unpinned takes a generic value, and `caveats` says what that
changes.** With no `sdp` pin the offer is a stock PCMU one, so a codec or
attribute the far end rejected does not appear. With an empty `pin` list the
response says that the scenario encodes no hypothesis. A pinned body brings the
captured `Content-Type` with it.

The `recv` sequence asserts what the capture actually held: every provisional
code seen, plus `100` whether or not the capture held one, and the final status.
A call with no final response in the capture asserts nothing about the outcome —
the scenario sends the request and waits.

For an INVITE the scenario sends an ACK either
way, with the Via that RFC 3261 calls for in each case: a fresh branch on a 2xx,
because that ACK is a new transaction, and `[last_Via:]` on a non-2xx, because
[RFC 3261 section 17.1.1.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3261.html#section-17.1.1.3) makes it
part of the INVITE transaction.

Twelve headers the scenario always owns come from the template whatever the
capture held, `pin: ["headers"]` included: `Via`, `Contact`, `Content-Length`,
`Content-Type`, `CSeq`, `From`, `To`, `Call-ID`, `Max-Forwards`, `Record-Route`,
`Route` and `User-Agent`. The template's `Via` and `Contact` name the host
running SIPp, so responses return to it.

Two escaping rules apply to captured text in the scenario. sipnab strips
control characters, CR and LF included, from captured header values. It splits
`]]>` inside a header value or SDP attribute across two CDATA sections, which
keeps the bytes exact.

Everything in `scenario` beyond the template — the Request-URI, header values,
SDP — came from the packet's sender. The response carries the provenance note
instead of fencing the scenario field by field. Review the scenario before
running it.

### `generate_wireshark_filter`

A display filter selecting one call, and the tshark line that applies it. Use
it to hand a call to someone who reads the capture in Wireshark.

| Name | Type | Legal values | If omitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `call_id` | string | A Call-ID the store holds. | Required — the call fails. |
| `include_media?` | bool? | `true` adds one `rtp.ssrc` term per stream attributed to the call. | `true`. |

```jsonc
// generate_wireshark_filter { "call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20" }
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "call_id": "1-1966@10.0.2.20",
  "display_filter": "sip.Call-ID == \"1-1966@10.0.2.20\" || rtp.ssrc == 0x343da99b",
  "tshark": "tshark -r 'tests/pcap-samples/sip-rtp-g711.pcap' -Y 'sip.Call-ID == \"1-1966@10.0.2.20\" || rtp.ssrc == 0x343da99b'",
  "streams_included": 1,
  "notes": [
    "rtp.ssrc matches only once Wireshark is decoding those packets as RTP. Enable 'Try to decode RTP outside of conversations', or use Decode As on the media ports, if the SSRC terms select nothing."
  ],
  "capture_identity": { "node": "capture-01", "instance": "cc2cb18df0ea68adfb9c9-2",
                        "dialog_generation": 13, "stream_generation": 2 },
  "source_exhausted": true,
  "source_stopped_early": false
}
```

The `tshark` line names this run's capture file when the server reads one, and
falls back to `<capture.pcap>` on a live capture. Both the filename and the
filter go through POSIX shell quoting, so an embedded quote in a Call-ID closes
and reopens the quoted word rather than ending it.

Read `notes` before using the filter:

- With `include_media: true` and no stream attributed to the call, it says the
  filter selects signaling only.
- With SSRC terms present, it says that `rtp.ssrc` matches nothing until
  Wireshark decodes those packets as RTP, and how to make it do so.

**A Call-ID carrying a control character fails.** A Wireshark display-filter
string literal escapes only `\` and `"`, so it cannot represent the Call-ID:

```jsonc
{ "code": -32602,
  "message": "this Call-ID carries the control character U+0009, which a Wireshark display-filter string literal cannot represent. A filter written around it would not mean what the Call-ID says." }
```
